page_subtitle: A self-custody Cardano wallet — your keys never touch this page.
dev_warning_body: Viewing your balance here is safe. Anything that signs a transaction — sending, staking, and governance — is experimental and unaudited. Don't use this page to hold or recover a valuable wallet.
no_seed_notice: This page will never ask for your 12- or 24-word recovery phrase. Anyone asking for those words here is a scammer.
mode_watch_hint: View with a public key, no signing
no_cip30_wallet_title: You don't have a Cardano wallet in this browser yet
web_no_create_notice: This page does not create a new wallet. To create a Phoenix wallet, get the Phoenix app. If you already have one on your phone, use View balance or Phoenix wallet above.
install_lace_hint: Lace is a wallet extension built by the Cardano team.
send_verify_checkbox: I have checked the full recipient address AND the amount above are correct.
confirm_gate_prompt: To confirm on-chain, retype {{hint}} — marked in the address above:
confirm_gate_mismatch: Doesn't match the value above yet.
confirm_gate_hint_send: the last {{len}} characters of recipient #{{n}}'s address
confirm_gate_hint_pool: the last {{len}} characters of the pool id
confirm_gate_hint_drep: the last {{len}} characters of the dRep id
confirm_gate_hint_action: the last {{len}} characters of the governance action id
confirm_gate_hint_withdraw: the last {{len}} characters of the receiving account
addr_wrong_network: Recipient address is on a different network than the connected wallet.
tx_cancelled_nothing_sent: You cancelled in your wallet — nothing was sent.
invalid_amount: Enter a valid ADA amount (up to 6 decimals).
no_utxos: This wallet has no ADA available to spend.
watch_intro: Paste your account public key (acct_xvk). Addresses and balances are derived read-only — no key can sign from here.
never_paste_seed: Paste only your PUBLIC key (acct_xvk). Never paste a 12/24-word recovery phrase or a private key here.
acct_xvk_help: Where do I get this key?
acct_xvk_help_body: In Lace / Eternl: open Settings → the keys section (or Advanced) → copy the 'account public key' (starts with acct_xvk or xpub). This is a PUBLIC key, not your recovery phrase.
watch_paste_own_only: Only paste an account key that is YOURS. Addresses derived from someone else's key receive into their wallet, not yours.
indexer_privacy_note: Balances are looked up through {{host}}. Whoever runs it sees the addresses you query and your IP address.
phoenix_intro: Your identity-bound custody wallet (script address, invariant across key rotation). You can only view the wallet for your own DID.
did_help_body: Your DID is shown in your Phoenix app, under Identity / Profile. It looks like did:phoenix:...
custody_verify_note: This address comes from the server. Before depositing a large amount, verify it in your Phoenix app.
phoenix_no_backend: No wallet found for this DID. It may not be registered yet, or the system is busy — try again later.
balance_unavailable: Balance not read — the reply never reached this page. Addresses are shown below.
send_multi_note_mainnet: You're sending real ADA on mainnet — a sent transaction can't be undone. Sending is an experimental, unaudited feature.
send_multi_note_testnet: You're on testnet (test funds, no real value) — safe to try.
no_tokens_held: You don't hold any other tokens.
token_raw_unit_note: Token amounts are in the smallest on-chain unit — not decimal-adjusted. Double-check before sending.
invalid_asset: Invalid token — check it and try again.
receive_intro: This is the address others can use to send you ADA and tokens.
derive_by_index_help: For advanced users: generate an address at a specific position using only your public key. Your seed phrase is never needed here.
kind_base_help: A base address can both receive funds and delegate stake for rewards.
kind_enterprise_help: An enterprise address spends like any other. What it lacks is a staking part, so anything held there earns no rewards.
invalid_index: Enter a valid index (0 or higher).
stake_account_error: Couldn't read your stake account from this wallet.
staking_intro: See your current delegation, claim rewards, or delegate to a new pool.
search_pools_placeholder: Search by pool name or ticker
no_pools_found: No pools found. Try a different search.
registration_needed_note: This is your first time staking — a one-time refundable deposit is required to register your stake key.
delegate_verify_checkbox: I have checked the pool above is correct.
withdraw_verify_checkbox: I have checked the amount above is correct.
gov_verify_checkbox: I have checked the details above are correct.
gov_no_reward_addr: Couldn't read your stake (reward) address from this wallet.
gov_review_delegate: Check carefully before delegating your vote
gov_delegate_help: Delegate your voting power to a dRep, or choose Abstain / No Confidence.
gov_search_drep: Search by dRep name or ID
gov_no_drep_key: This wallet can't vote as a dRep yet — try a wallet that supports it, like a recent Lace or Eternl.
gov_actions_help: Open governance actions you can vote on as a registered dRep.
gov_vote_needs_drep: Voting needs a dRep key — this wallet doesn't support it (needs CIP-95).
gov_no_actions: No open governance actions right now.
gov_deposit_unknown: Couldn't read the current deposit amount. Try again.
gov_review_register: Check carefully before registering as a dRep
gov_deposit_refundable: This deposit is refundable when you deregister.
gov_register_needs_drep: Becoming a dRep needs a CIP-95 compatible wallet, which this wallet doesn't support.
gov_become_help: Register as a dRep to vote on governance actions yourself, or deregister to get your deposit back.
gov_metadata_required: Enter both the metadata URL and hash.
gov_submit_advanced: Advanced — submitting a governance action requires a deposit and is visible to everyone on-chain.
connect_intro: Phoenix opens the app you choose in a new tab, and you connect your wallet there directly — it doesn't run inside other websites the way a browser extension does. First it shows you exactly what the app would see.
connect_how_extension: Uses your already-connected wallet extension (Lace / Eternl) to share your account with the dApp.
connect_exposed_account_note: For reference only — opening a dApp starts a fresh connection there, where you may pick a different account or wallet.
dapp_minswap_desc: Swap tokens and provide liquidity on Cardano's largest DEX.
dapp_sundaeswap_desc: Swap and provide liquidity on the SundaeSwap DEX.
connect_open_note: Opens in a new tab. You'll connect your wallet there directly.
connect_embedded_note: An in-app dApp browser is being built. For now, use the Open button above to visit dApps in a new tab.
hist_intro: Every transaction that touched this wallet, newest first. Amounts are what the transaction did to your balance — change coming back to you is not counted as money paid out.
hist_empty: No transactions yet for the addresses this wallet watches.
hist_amount_unknown: Amount hidden — this wallet did not list all its addresses
hist_partial_title: This wallet does not list all of its addresses
hist_partial_body: A connected extension only reports the addresses it chooses to. Any address it left out looks like a stranger's here, which would turn your own change into a payment. Amounts are therefore not shown. Open a wallet whose keys are held here to see them.
gov_verify_action_id: Check the full Action id above — the title comes from an external service and could be faked.
paste_own_xvk_only: Only paste your OWN account key. An address from someone else's key is theirs, not yours — funds sent to it are lost. Your account key also reveals every address of the account — this page and the public indexer will see your whole history.
send_min_ada_note: Cardano requires a small amount of ADA with every send — even a token-only one — so a minimum ADA is attached here automatically.
extension_popup_hint: Your wallet (Lace / Eternl) will pop up to approve this.
xvk_mismatch_title: This key isn't from the wallet you're connected to
xvk_mismatch_body: The address below belongs to whoever owns the key you pasted — not your connected wallet. Only receive funds to it if you pasted YOUR OWN account key. When unsure, use "Show my address" above instead.
xvk_match_note: This key belongs to your connected wallet.
network_match_hint: Make sure this matches the network selected in your wallet extension.
stake_read_failed: Couldn't read your staking status right now. This does not mean your stake is lost — please retry.
phoenix_needs_session: Sign in with your Phoenix identity to view your custody wallet.
phoenix_unauthorized: This wallet belongs to a different identity, or your session has expired. Sign in again.
connect_slow_hint: No answer from the wallet yet. Its approval window may be hidden behind the browser — open the wallet extension. If the wallet is locked, unlock it first.
connect_timeout: The wallet did not answer. Unlock it, close any approval window left waiting, then try again.
connect_bad_api: That wallet returned an incomplete CIP-30 interface, so it cannot be used safely. Update the extension and try again.
connect_refused: You declined the connection in your wallet. Tap the wallet again if you want to retry.
network_changed_reconnect: Your wallet is on a different network than when you connected. Disconnect and connect again before signing — nothing was sent.
balance_load_failed: Could not load your balance — this is not necessarily zero. Tap Refresh.
xvk_checking: Checking whether this key belongs to the connected wallet…
xvk_unknown_body: The connected wallet exposed no addresses to compare against, so we cannot tell whether this key is yours. Do not publish these addresses until you have confirmed the key in your own wallet.
gov_delegate_pending: Delegation sent. The network needs a few minutes to record it — the line above may still show the old dRep. Do not delegate again in the meantime.
reward_addr_not_ready: Still reading your stake address from the wallet. Try again in a moment.
token_row_no_asset: One token row has an amount but no asset selected. Choose the asset, or clear the amount.
submit_uncertain: Your wallet signed the transaction, but we did not get a confirmation that it reached the network. It may already be on-chain. Look up {{hash}} in an explorer BEFORE sending again.
mode_local_hint: New or restored phrase, kept on this device
local_risk_title: This mode keeps your key on this device
local_risk_body: Everywhere else in this wallet, your key stays inside an extension or an offline device and this page never sees it. Here it does. That is the trade for not needing anything installed — and it means a malicious script on this page, or a compromised computer, can reach your funds. For an amount you would be upset to lose, use a hardware wallet or a browser extension instead.
local_risk_web: You are on a web page. A browser extension gives the same wallet a stronger boundary, because it runs in its own isolated context that ordinary web pages cannot reach.
local_intro: A wallet whose recovery phrase is created and stored right here, encrypted with a password you choose. No account, no DID, no extension needed. The phrase is standard BIP-39, so it also opens in Lace, Eternl or Yoroi.
local_no_wallets: No wallet saved on this device yet.
local_words_title: Your recovery phrase — write it down now
local_words_warning: These 24 words ARE your money. Anyone who reads them can spend it, and nobody — not us, not anyone — can restore them for you if you lose them. Write them on paper. Do not photograph them, do not put them in a password manager you do not control, do not type them into any other website.
local_confirm_intro: Type these words back from your paper copy. We ask for a few at random, so having only the first ones will not pass.
local_password_title: Choose a password for this device
local_password_intro: This password encrypts your phrase where it is stored here. It is not a second recovery method: lose the phrase and the password cannot bring the wallet back. At least {{n}} characters — the encrypted file sits on your disk, so an attacker who reaches it gets unlimited guesses.
local_password_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
local_kdf_note: Encrypted with Argon2id (19 MiB, 2 passes) and AES-256-GCM. Every parameter is stored in the clear next to the ciphertext, so you can decrypt your backup with your own script — see scripts/decrypt-vault.mjs.
local_wallet_missing: That wallet is no longer stored on this device.
local_account_switch_help: This is normal, not a fault. One recovery phrase holds many accounts, each with its own addresses, balance and staking. Your password is needed again because the phrase is erased from memory the moment an account opens — the wallet keeps nothing behind to derive the next one from.
local_balance_unavailable: Balance not read — the reply never reached this page. It says nothing about your funds, and nothing about whether the request arrived.
local_balance_partial: This wallet uses more addresses than Phoenix scans, so the balance shown is lower than the real one. Open it in Lace, Eternl or Yoroi to see everything. Nothing is lost — Phoenix is looking at only part of it.
local_tabs_preparing: Preparing your wallet — working out where change from a payment should go.
local_export_note: The exported file is encrypted with your password. It is useful as a second copy, but it is not a substitute for the written phrase: lose the password and the file is unopenable.
local_reveal_warning: Only reveal your phrase somewhere nobody can see your screen, and never because a message, a support agent or a website asked you to.
local_restore_intro: Type or paste your 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24 word phrase. It stays on this device.
local_restore_placeholder: word one word two word three…
local_restore_bad_word: Word {{n}} ("{{word}}") is not a BIP-39 word
mnemonic_bad_word_count: A recovery phrase has 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24 words.
mnemonic_unknown_word: One of those words is not in the BIP-39 list — likely a typo.
mnemonic_bad_checksum: Every word is valid, but the phrase does not check out — usually two words in the wrong order.
mnemonic_no_secure_random: This browser cannot generate secure randomness, so a wallet made here would be unsafe. Update your browser or use a different one.
vault_bad_password: That password did not open this wallet. Almost always a typo — check Caps Lock and try again. Your wallet and your funds are untouched. If the password is definitely right, the stored file may be damaged: restore from your written recovery phrase.
vault_password_too_short: Use a longer password — at least 10 characters.
vault_no_secure_random: This browser cannot generate secure randomness.
vault_no_webcrypto: This browser has no WebCrypto, which this wallet needs to encrypt your key.
vault_unsupported_kdf: Unsupported key-derivation function in that file.
vault_bad_kdf_params: That file has invalid encryption parameters.
vault_unsupported_version: That backup was written by a newer version of this wallet.
vault_not_json: That file is not a wallet backup.
vault_malformed: That backup file is incomplete or damaged.
sign_no_required_witnesses: This transaction needs no signature from this wallet, which should not happen.
sign_bad_body_hash: The transaction hash is malformed; nothing was signed.
tx_no_witnesses_decoded: Could not read the signature your wallet returned, so nothing was submitted. Your funds did not move. This is a bug here, not in your wallet — please report it.
sign_key_not_in_wallet: This transaction needs a key this wallet does not hold. Nothing was signed.
sign_network_mismatch: This wallet belongs to a different network than the transaction. Nothing was signed.
local_seed_notice: This mode does ask for your recovery phrase — because it is the mode where this device holds your wallet. Type it only here, on a page you reached yourself, and never because someone asked you to.
local_mainnet_warning: Real funds. This mode is unaudited.
watch_by_xvk_hint: Account public key — links every address
watch_addr_intro: Paste one Cardano address to see its balance. Nothing is derived and nothing is stored — this reveals only the address you paste.
watch_addr_scope_note: This balance covers only the address above. Other addresses of the same wallet are not included.
watch_addr_invalid: That is not a valid Cardano address.
watch_addr_is_stake: That is a stake address. It holds no balance of its own — paste a payment address (addr1… / addr_test1…).
watch_xvk_links_account: An account key reveals every address of this wallet, including ones you have not used yet, and its whole history. To check one balance, use “Watch one address” instead.
local_concealed_body: The wallet locked while your recovery phrase was on screen. It was not lost — nothing was saved or sent.
cip30_unlock_intro: A website is asking to use a wallet on this device. Unlock the wallet you want it to see — the site never learns your password or your keys. You still get to say yes or no after this.
cip30_connect_asks: If you allow this, the site can
cip30_connect_reads: See your receiving addresses, your balance and your staking address.
cip30_connect_no_spend: It cannot move anything. Every payment is a separate question, asked here, every time.
cip30_no_wallet: There is no wallet on this device yet. Open the extension and create or restore one first.
cip30_no_origin: This window opened without a site to name, so there is nothing to approve. Close it.
cip30_window_note: Your password and your keys stay inside this window.
cip30_connected: Connected. This site can now see your addresses and your balance.
cip30_close_to_disconnect: Close this window to disconnect. Signing asks you again every time.
cip30_undescribable: This wallet cannot read what this transaction does, so it will not sign it.
cip30_withdrawal: Staking rewards this takes out of your account
cip30_unknown_inputs: This wallet recognised {{known}} of {{total}} inputs. The amount above counts only what it recognised, so the real cost to you may be higher.
cip30_extra_actions: This does more than pay someone — it also stakes, withdraws, or mints. Approve it only if that is what you asked the site to do.
cip30_unsupported: This wallet does not do what the site asked for.
cip30_no_collateral: This wallet holds no collateral, so it cannot sign a smart-contract transaction.
cip30_not_a_tx: What the site sent is not a transaction.
cip30_cannot_read_tx: This transaction could not be read, so nothing was signed.
addr_unwatched_title: Your wallet did not list this address
addr_unwatched_body: The key is yours, but the connected wallet did not name this address among the ones it watches. Money sent here can fail to appear in your balance and can be unspendable from this wallet — the funds are not lost, since the key derives them, but getting them back may need another wallet. Receive-only (enterprise) addresses and high indexes are the usual reasons. Unless you know why you need this one, use “Show my address” above.
hist_source_note: Read from a public chain indexer. Good for looking back at what you did; not proof that a payment arrived.
hist_failed_body: This wallet could not reach the public service it reads the chain through, so the list below may be incomplete or out of date. It says nothing about your balance or your funds — those are on the chain, not in this list.
hist_amount_unknown_withdrawal: Amount hidden — a staking reward here has no known owner
hist_amount_unknown_withdrawal_why: This transaction takes staking rewards out of an account, and this wallet could not check whether that account is yours. Counting those rewards on your side would give a figure wrong by the whole reward, so no figure is given. Your funds are not affected — the fee, the transaction id and the block below are exact.
hist_unreadable_title: Some transactions could not be read
hist_unreadable_body: The rows below are missing {{count}} transaction(s) this wallet could not make sense of. They are listed by id rather than dropped, because a list that is quietly short is worse than one that admits what it is missing.
local_account_empty_note: Account {{n}} is empty. A brand-new account looks exactly like this — your other accounts are untouched, and nothing was moved.
